rules.summary: A health care provider may not bill a sexual assault survivor for any part of a forensic exam, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, or a denied insurance claim.
rules.quote: A health care provider shall not submit a bill for any portion of the costs of a sexual assault medical forensic examination to the victim of the sexual assault, including any insurance deductible or co-pay, denial of claim by an insurer, or any other out-of-pocket expense.

rules.summary: The provider must tell the survivor, orally and in writing, that the exam will not be billed to their insurance without their express written consent, and they may decline for privacy or safety reasons.
rules.quote: Advise the victim, orally and in writing, that a claim shall not be submitted to his or her insurance carrier without his or her express written consent, and that he or she may decline to consent if he or she believes that submitting a claim to the insurance carrier would substantially interfere with his or her personal privacy or safety.

rules.summary: The Crime Victim Services Commission pays the provider up to $1,200 for a sexual assault forensic exam.
rules.quote: The commission shall pay a health care provider not more than $1,200.00 for the cost of performing a sexual assault medical forensic examination

rules.summary: If billing insurance would threaten the survivor's privacy or safety, the provider can bill SAFE Response for the exam instead.
rules.quote: If a victim believes submitting a claim to their insurance carrier would substantially interfere with his or her personal privacy or safety, the doctor or nurse can bill SAFE Response for the forensic examination.

params.payer: Crime Victim Services Commission, or another entity other than the victim, when insurance cannot be billed or does not pay

rules.summary: If the victim's insurance does not pay or is not available, the provider can seek payment from the commission or another entity, but never from the victim.
rules.quote: A health care provider may seek payment from 1 or both of the following if reimbursement cannot be obtained from the victim's insurance or insurance is unavailable: (a) The commission under this section. (b) From another entity other than the victim.

rules.summary: The total award cannot exceed $45,000 per claimant.
rules.quote: The aggregate award under this act must not exceed $45,000.00 per claimant.

rules.summary: Counseling with a licensed or registered therapist or counselor is reimbursed at up to $80 per hourly session.
rules.quote: The maximum hourly reimbursement rate must not exceed $80.00 per hourly session for a therapist or counselor licensed or registered to practice in this state

rules.summary: Counseling with a licensed psychologist or physician is reimbursed at up to $125 per hourly session.
rules.quote: except that the maximum hourly reimbursement rate must not exceed $125.00 per hourly session for a psychologist or physician licensed to practice in this state.

rules.summary: Counseling is limited to 35 sessions per person plus up to 20 family sessions, at $80 per hour for a therapist or counselor and $125 per hour for a psychologist or physician.
rules.quote: 35 sessions, 20 family sessions $80/hour for a therapist/counselor $125/hour for a psychologist/physician
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS award limits table, Psychological Counseling

rules.summary: Lost earnings are paid at the actual loss, up to $1,000 for each week.
rules.quote: An award must not exceed $1,000.00 for each week of lost earnings.

rules.summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $3,800 per claimant.
rules.quote: An award for expenses under this subdivision may not exceed $3,800.00 per claimant.

rules.summary: Transportation for trips of 50 miles or less each way is capped at $1,000 in total per claimant.
rules.quote: (i) If the expense is for travel of a distance of not more than 50 miles each way from the claimant's residence, $1,000.00.

rules.summary: Transportation is capped at $5,000 in total per claimant when the trip is at least 50 miles each way to care that is not available within 50 miles of home.
rules.quote: (ii) If the expense is for travel that meets 1 or more of the following, $5,000.00: (A) If the travel is a distance of not less than 50 miles from the claimant's residence each way and is to and from a health care provider, mental health professional as that term is defined in section 100b of the mental health code, 1974 PA 258, MCL 330.1100b, or health facility or agency that renders a specific treatment or care that is not available within 50 miles of the claimant's residence.

rules.summary: Residential security (security systems, window or lock repair or replacement, added locks) is covered up to $1,000 per residence.
rules.quote: (f) Reasonable costs of not more than $1,000.00 per residence for installing, increasing, or replacing residential security, which may include installing a home security device or system; replacing or repairing windows or locks; or increasing the number of locks

rules.summary: Clothing or bedding held as evidence can be replaced up to $250.
rules.quote: (j) Replacement costs of not more than $250.00 for clothing or bedding of an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), (b), (e), or (f), that is held as evidence of a crime.

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup at a home or vehicle is covered up to $5,000 per crime scene.
rules.quote: the crime scene cleanup services resulting from a crime for that residence or vehicle after crime scene cleanup is permitted by the investigating law enforcement agency, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00 per crime scene.

rules.summary: Unreimbursed medical care for the victim is covered.
rules.quote: (a) Medical care for the victim or intervenor.

rules.summary: Psychological counseling is covered, subject to the session and rate limits.
rules.quote: (b) Subject to subsection (6), psychological or grief counseling for an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), (b), (c), (e), (f), or (g).

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered, including time off work to seek medical care, recover, get counseling, or get help from a victim services organization.
rules.quote: A claimant may be awarded for loss of earnings under this subsection for lost wages as a result of the crime

rules.summary: Temporary or permanent relocation is covered when the move protects the survivor's safety or emotional or financial well-being, and generally must happen within 1 year of the crime or of a new threat unless good cause is shown.
rules.quote: An award for expenses under this subdivision may be made only if the claimant is relocating to protect the claimant's physical safety or emotional or financial well-being as a result of the crime and, unless good cause is shown, is relocating within 1 year of the date the crime occurred, or of the date the claimant is threatened by a change in circumstance or by an indicator of danger.

rules.summary: As part of relocation, temporary lodging is covered for up to 30 days.
rules.quote: (iii) Costs for temporary lodging for not more than 30 days.

rules.summary: Relocation can include the first month of rent, a security deposit, and the cost of starting utilities at the new home.
rules.quote: (i) The first month of rent, a security deposit, and the costs to start utilities in the dwelling unit to which the claimant relocates.

rules.summary: Transportation is covered to reach victim services, medical care, or mental health care.
rules.quote: (e) Transportation expenses for the purpose of an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), or if the victim or intervenor is deceased, for a person listed in section 4(1)(b), (e), or (f), to access services from a victim services organization, medical care, or mental health care, or to attend the funeral of a victim or intervenor.

rules.summary: Replacement services such as child care and homemaking are covered when the survivor cannot do them because of the injury or while attending victim services.
rules.quote: (d) Replacement services for homemaking tasks, child care, and other services previously performed by an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), (b), (e), or (f), that, because of the victim's injury, or the claimant's attendance at a victim services organization to receive services related to the crime, must temporarily or permanently be performed by another person.

rules.summary: Reasonable and necessary medical, dental, optical, and counseling costs are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable and necessary medical, dental, optical, counseling, and non-medical remedial treatment.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that May Be Covered

rules.summary: Eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, and other prescription devices are covered if damaged during or needed because of the crime.
rules.quote: Eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetic devices, or other prescription devices, if damaged during or needed because of the crime.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that May Be Covered

params.extension: The commission may extend the deadline for good cause on the claimant's petition (MCL 18.355(3)); for criminal sexual conduct against a minor, police-records-based rules allow filing within 5 years after the crime was reported (MCL 18.355(2)(a)).

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 5 years after the crime.
rules.quote: a claim must be filed by the claimant not later than 5 years after the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based

rules.summary: For criminal sexual conduct (first through third degree) where police records show the victim was under 18, a claim may be filed within 5 years after the crime was reported, if reported before age 28 or later with good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: a claim based on the crime of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree may be filed by a claimant not later than 5 years after the crime was reported: (i) Police records show the victim of the crime was less than 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence and the victim reported the crime before attaining 28 years of age. (ii) Police records show the victim of the crime was less than 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence, the victim reported the crime after attaining 28 years of age, and the claimant shows that there was good cause for the delay in reporting the crime.

rules.summary: The commission may extend the filing deadline for good cause if the claimant asks.
rules.quote: Upon petition by the claimant and for good cause shown, the commission may extend the period in which a claim may be filed under subsection (2).

rules.summary: For sexual assault, having a sexual assault forensic exam satisfies the prompt police-reporting and cooperation requirements for compensation.
rules.quote: For payments authorized under this section or for payments made to victims under section 6, administration to the victim of a sexual assault medical forensic examination satisfies the requirements for prompt law enforcement reporting and victim cooperation under sections 6 and 10.

rules.summary: In general, police records must show the crime was reported to the proper authorities.
rules.quote: (c) Police records show that the crime was reported to the proper authorities.

rules.summary: The program says a sexual assault forensic exam may be used in place of a police report.
rules.quote: The crime must be reported to law enforcement (waivers may apply). If the crime was a sexual assault, then a sexual assault forensic exam may be used in lieu of reporting to police.

rules.summary: A claim needs at least $200 in out-of-pocket loss or at least 5 days of lost earnings or support; the commission may waive this for victims of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree.
rules.quote: An award must not be made on a claim unless the claimant has incurred an out-of-pocket loss of not less than $200.00, or has lost at least 5 days' earnings or support, but the commission may waive the limitations of this subsection if a claimant is retired by reason of age or disability. If the claimant is a victim of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree, the commission may waive the limitations of this subsection.

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, insurance, or public funds received for the injury.
rules.quote: An award must be reduced by the amount of 1 or more of the following payments received or to be received as a result of the injury:

rules.summary: The program is the payer of last resort, so insurance and other public funds must be used first.
rules.quote: Please note that Crime Victim Compensation is the payer of last resort. This means that your private insurance or other public funds, if available, must be utilized first in order for you to be eligible for compensation.

rules.summary: Having insurance does not disqualify you; the program can cover copays and deductibles.

rules.summary: The commission must consider whether the victim's misconduct contributed to the injury and may reduce or reject the award on that basis.
rules.quote: the commission shall determine whether the victim's misconduct contributed to his or her injury and shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with the determination.

rules.summary: A claim is rejected if the commission finds willful noncooperation with law enforcement or the prosecutor; for sexual assault, a forensic exam satisfies the cooperation requirement (see MI-REPORT-1).
rules.quote: In the event of determination of willful noncooperation by the victim or other claimant, the commission shall reject the claim.

rules.summary: If an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, the commission may make an emergency award of up to $4,000, which is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of an emergency award under this section must not exceed $4,000.00 and must be deducted from the final award made to the claimant.

rules.summary: Sexual assault victims are listed as eligible for crime victim compensation.

rules.summary: Personal injury includes bodily harm (including pregnancy) and psychological, mental, or emotional injury from a perceived or actual threat.

coverage.notes: No statutory time limit for reporting to police was found in MCL 18.360 or the program pages saved here, so within_days is left out. Michigan administrative rules were not searched or saved; all caps come from MCL 18.361, 18.359, and 18.355a. Counseling has two hourly rates (therapist/counselor vs psychologist/physician), recorded as separate expense_cap rules. No processing time is stated in the saved program pages, application, checklist, or reference guide; the checklist only says timely submission of documents may reduce processing time, so no processing_time rule was added.

researcher_notes: Statute text is from legislature.mi.gov (current through 2022 PA 77 and 78, effective Aug. 12, 2023). The MDHHS SAFE Response page says that for injuries other than the forensic exam, a victim 'would have to' report to police to get compensation, while MCL 18.355a(10) says a forensic exam satisfies prompt reporting and cooperation for payments under section 6, and the MDHHS Do I Qualify page says an exam may be used in lieu of a police report. The statute wins; Tend should rely on MI-REPORT-1. MCL 18.355a(10) also says a survivor cannot be required to participate in the criminal justice system or cooperate with law enforcement to receive a forensic exam. The minimum-loss waiver for criminal sexual conduct is discretionary ('may waive'). Security cap is per residence and crime scene cleanup cap is per crime scene, so params.per uses 'residence' and 'crime_scene', which are not in the schema's per list. The FAQ and brochure say the program does not cover pain and suffering; the forensic exam payment to providers is capped at $1,200 (with up to $700 of that for facility and exam fees) and is separate from the victim's own compensation claim. The federal OVC directory lists the compensation office line as 517-241-7373; the victims-only toll-free line 877-251-7373 is on the MDHHS program page. Reviewer: the saved sources do not say whether the $45,000 aggregate cap and the 2022 PA 77 caps apply to crimes that happened before Aug. 12, 2023 (the agency page says the limit was recently raised from $25,000). MI-CAP-4 (agency table) matches the statutory 35-session and 20-family-session limits in MCL 18.361(6). Filing: the Applying for Compensation page says applications should be submitted electronically when possible, by email (MDHHS-MichiganCrimeVictim@Michigan.gov) or fax (517-335-2439), and can still be mailed; there is no online portal and no in-person drop-off is stated. The application PDF (DCH-0560, Rev. 1-26, MI-S15) is fillable with 202 AcroForm fields and says the previous edition may be used. Required documents come from the English Application Checklist (Revised 02/2025, MI-S18); several apply only to specific benefits (relocation, lost earnings, funeral, loss of support), so each required_document rule carries an expense or note saying when it applies. The checklist also lists two cost estimates and a prescription for rehabilitative equipment if disabled by the injury; that item was not added as a separate rule.
